findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "filter_jobs" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_jobs, get_job, get_company, filter_jobs, similar_jobs, search_by_meaning · Private data: search_jobs, get_job, get_company, search_by_meaning · Public sink: search_by_meaning.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_jobs, get_job, get_company, filter_jobs, similar_jobs, search_by_meaning · Private data: search_jobs, get_job, get_company, search_by_meaning · Public sink: search_by_meaning

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_jobs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
